instructions: Trim off any thick pieces of hard fat from the 3 lbs short ribs. Put them in a large bowl, cover them with cold water and leave them for 30 minutes to draw out the blood. At the same time, put 4 of the dried shiitake in a small bowl and cover them with warm water.
Meanwhile, cut the onion in half. Peel the ginger, cut 4 thin coins from it and grate 1 tsp from the rest. Cut the white parts off 2 of the scallions and keep the green parts for the end.
Bring 5 cups water to a boil in a large heavy pot over high heat. Add one onion half, the 4 ginger coins, 5 of the garlic cloves and the 2 scallion whites.
Drain the ribs and add them to the pot. When it comes back to a boil, skim off the gray foam with a spoon. Turn the heat down to medium high and boil the ribs for 10 minutes.

Lift the ribs out onto a plate. Pour the stock through a strainer into a large bowl and throw away the onion, ginger, garlic and scallion. Let the stock sit for a few minutes so the fat rises, then spoon off as much of it as you can. Rinse out the pot.

In a bowl, grate half the Asian pear and the other onion half. Mince the last 3 garlic cloves into it, then add the grated ginger, 1/2 cup soy sauce, 2 tbsp sugar, 2 tbsp honey, 1/4 cup mirin and the 1/2 tsp black pepper. Stir until the sugar dissolves.

Put the ribs back in the pot, pour the sauce over them and stir to coat. Add 2 1/2 cups of the stock and keep the rest nearby. Cover, bring it to a boil over medium heat, then let it bubble steadily for 25 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel the radish and cut it into 1 1/2 inch chunks. Peel the carrot and cut it into 1 inch chunks. Squeeze the water out of the shiitake, cut off the stems and quarter the caps.
Stir the radish, carrot and mushrooms into the ribs. Cover and cook for 20 minutes more.

While that cooks, rinse the 2 cups rice in a few changes of water until the water runs mostly clear. Cook it in a rice cooker, or in a covered pot with 2 1/4 cups water over low heat for 18 minutes, then leave it covered off the heat for 10 minutes.

Add 6 of the chestnuts to the ribs and take the lid off. Boil for about 10 minutes more, stirring gently now and then, until the sauce has thickened enough to coat the ribs and a fork slides into the meat easily while it still holds onto the bone. If the sauce gets too thick before the meat is ready, add a splash of the saved stock.
Thinly slice the 2 scallion greens. Turn off the heat, then gently stir in the scallion greens and the 2 tbsp sesame oil.
Taste the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: All three read versions soak the ribs in cold water, parboil them and skim before the braise, and none of them sears the meat first. Korean Bapsang parboils with onion, ginger, garlic and scallion and braises in that defatted stock with a soy, sugar, honey, rice wine and grated pear sauce, adding radish, carrot and dried shiitake partway through and chestnuts, jujubes and ginkgo nuts for the last 10 minutes. Beyond Kimchee blends kiwi into the sauce and uses a kelp stock, and Takes Two Eggs adds potatoes. This one follows Korean Bapsang, keeps chestnuts as the one garnish nut and serves it with rice. Korean Bapsang notes the ribs can be prepared up to the braise the day before.
